observations: A blocky rectangular head fills most of the warm brown field; the left eye is a tight spiral of orange and yellow rings while the right eye zone is filled with crossing black hatches inside a looser rectangle.
A wide red-outlined mouth sits in the lower third, its interior showing four white rectangular teeth against a dark gap, anchored by thick red bars top and bottom.
Along the top edge, a dense row of white zigzag lines runs the full width, with loose yellow and pink coils spilling outward left and right above the head.
reading: The brown field pushes the head forward rather than letting it float. Two eye zones refuse to match: one pulls inward through concentric rings, the other deflects through crossed lines — a split that reads as unease rather than symmetry. The red-framed mouth, tooth-heavy with a visible dark gap between the bars, tips the mood toward something between a shout and a grimace. The zigzag crown adds a restless border that keeps the whole form from settling.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, #18 shares the blocky head format and red-outlined mouth with its immediate neighbor nnxyz nifty faces #19, but swaps that work's bright cyan field and matched spiral eyes for a warm brown ground and mismatched eye treatments — a contrast that sharpens both works when seen together.

connections.reason: Both works use a red-outlined mouth with white teeth as the dominant lower anchor, but #19 pairs matched spiral eyes on a dark purple ground while #18 splits its eye treatment across a brown field — the structural similarity and tonal difference are visible at once.

In #17 the head tilts and opens onto a flat cyan field with lines flying outward, whereas #18 keeps the head upright and contained against brown with lines that loop back inward — the same dense layering used in opposite spatial directions.

lookingQuestion: The two eye zones are built from completely different line strategies — what does following each one separately, without moving to the other, reveal about how the overall face holds together?
ambiguities: Title-derived and recorded-creation order align for this work, but gaps exist elsewhere in the owned subset, so neither order can be treated as a complete making sequence.
